messages:
Maya: heads up — bringing up a HF spm model for Redwood QA, hit a confusing token-id shift during hf->redwood conversion.
Liam: hmm, short repro? which script you ran?
Maya: `scripts/hf_to_redwood.py --sentencepiece --emit-vocab` then load into runtime.
Chen: can you paste the tokenizer config.json you got from HF?
Maya: sure — snippet:
```json
{"add_bos_token": false, "unk_token": "<unk>", "eos_token": "</s>", "vocab_size": 32768}
```
Liam: classic: HF spm models often assume special tokens are handled by SentencePiece merges/reserved ids. what did your converted vocab show for `</s>`?
Maya: two entries. `</s>` mapped at id=1 and id=32767 after conversion. generated outputs sometimes truncate early.
Chen: that smells like merge-order reindexing. when we rewrite merges in bpe space we can accidentally duplicate surface tokens if spm's control symbols collide with suffixpiece entries.
Eva: did you try `--preserve-special-token-ids` flag? We added that to the converter to keep HF reserved indices intact.
Maya: tried it, converter warns: `collision detected: reserved '</s>' present in vocab and merges` then proceeds and duplicates.
Liam: can you paste a tiny diff from `vocab.txt` (lines around the specials)?
Maya: pasted:
```
0 <pad>
1 </s>
2 <unk>
...
32766 er
32767 </s>
```
Liam: yup — duplicate `</s>` at top and end. runtime assumes first occurrence = EOS, but we index into kv cache by the other index sometimes, so KV offsets shift -> decoder reads wrong past keys -> hallucinations/early stop.
Zane: ran a quick eval on small prompt set, Rouge-L dropped 3.6 pts vs native HF baseline. replication steps: convert -> load model -> run 50 prompts -> compare.
Chen: root cause: SentencePiece sometimes exposes control symbols both as normal tokens and as dedicated `VOCAB` entries depending on training flags. our converter must dedupe by surface form and remap token ids in model and merges atomically.
Eva: short-term patch: detect duplicates in `vocab.txt` and pick the lower id as canonical, then rewrite model's token embeddings to collapse duplicate slot (sum or copy) and remap merge indices. risk: breaks deterministic ids for downstream evals.
Maya: I pushed a tiny fix to branch `spm-dedupe-fix` that 1) scans for duplicate surface tokens, 2) emits warning, 3) rewrites merges and `config.json` to canonicalize `eos_token` index. sample command: `python tools/spm_fix.py --vocab vocab.txt --out fixed_vocab.txt --map remap.json`
Liam: nice. can we add an automated check in onboarding CI to fail on duplicates? quick test: `python -c "import collections,sys;print([t for t,c in collections.Counter(open('vocab.txt').read().splitlines()).items() if c>1])"`
Maya: added a unit in PR, plus a small integration test that loads the model after conversion and runs 5 short prompts to assert no early-EOS.
Zane: also saw `add_bos_token` mismatch with chat-template instantiation. HF model lacked BOS so our chat template prepends one -> off-by-one in past_key_values indexing. add that to the checklist.
Chen: doc note: when onboarding SPM -> BPE we must verify: special token uniqueness, add_bos/add_eos semantics, merge-table ordering preserved, and rerun tokenization on canonical test prompts comparing token id sequences.
Maya: action items: (1) merge spm-dedupe-fix (2) add CI duplicate check + toy prompts (3) re-run quant eval after remap and compare latency/quality.
Eva: thanks — I'll take quant eval once PR is merged.
oncall-bot: Deployed test-runner job `onboarding-smoke` queued (job id: 6421).
Liam: great, keep notes in the model onboarding doc. :+1:
Maya: thanks all — saved us a weird regression. :relieved:
